scene_timeline.visual_description: Creator @crsnscott speaks to the camera with a screenshot of his Substack post '25 THINGS FOR FREELANCE CREATIVES' overlaid.
scene_timeline.audio_description: Probably my greatest contribution to society was the Substack that I wrote today.
scene_timeline.text_on_screen:
ORANGE TREE STUDIO
25 THINGS FOR FREELANCE CREATIVES
Business tools, hacks, mockups, tutorials, inspiration, and more.
SEP 10, 2025

scene_timeline.visual_description: Creator scrolls through the 'Inspiration & Organization' section of the list.
scene_timeline.audio_description: It is essentially just a list of 25 things I wish I had when I started from inspiration and organization...
scene_timeline.text_on_screen:
Inspiration & Organization
1. Cosmos — like Pinterest, but much better...
2. Framer — next level templates for portfolios or websites
3. Milanote — free, easy to build mood boards...
4. Internet Archive — good ol flickr. very unique old archives
5. Notion — organize projects, clients, and inspiration...

scene_timeline.visual_description: Creator scrolls through the 'YouTube University' section.
scene_timeline.audio_description: ...to the YouTube videos I learned Illustrator to the YouTubes I watch today to how to be a studio owner and grow.
scene_timeline.text_on_screen:
YouTube University
6. The Futur — straight talk on design & business...
7. EdgyKatrina — beginner friendly Adobe illustrator tutorials...
8. Orenmeetsworld — dude has seen behind the curtain...
9. Jesse Nyberg — talented graphic designer showing process...
10. Tetragrammaton — my king, Rick Rubin, talking to the author that changed my life, Steven Pressfield

scene_timeline.visual_description: Creator scrolls through the 'Mockup Madness' section.
scene_timeline.audio_description: Um, all the mockup sites that I use for clients...
scene_timeline.text_on_screen:
Mockup Madness
11. MockupWorld — free mockups to show off your designs in context
12. Envato Elements — unlimited mockups for a monthly fee
13. Bendito Mockups — very elite site, good freebies but mostly paid
14. Moxio Studio — need Adobe stock account, but 77 pages of mockups
15. Mockup Maison — limited freebies, but very high quality paid mockups

scene_timeline.visual_description: Creator scrolls through the 'Big Business' section.
scene_timeline.audio_description: ...and even some business stuff like contracts, invoicing, positioning tips...
scene_timeline.text_on_screen:
Big Business
16. Hello Bonsai — free, lawyer-reviewed templates and more
17. Zoho — simple, professional invoicing & expense tracking...
18. Loom — record quick video walkthroughs for clients...
19. Positioning Tip — "I design brand identities for wellness founders" > "I do logos for everyone."
20. Client Onboarding Tip — always send a welcome PDF...

scene_timeline.visual_description: Creator scrolls through the 'Portfolio Project Prompts' section.
scene_timeline.audio_description: ...and then at the end I give you some portfolio project prompts.
scene_timeline.text_on_screen:
Portfolio Project Prompts
21. Design packaging for an unrealistic product. EX: "Cereal to make you taller"
22. Take 3 random objects from your house and design a product label for them.
23. Design your own currency. $$$

scene_timeline.visual_description: Creator returns to full-screen talking head, pointing to the link in his bio and encouraging subscriptions.
scene_timeline.audio_description: Again, that is on my Substack right now. It is free for all readers... please subscribe... I'm going to be shooting for every Wednesday on resources, lessons, templates... whatever it is to possibly help you guys succeed.
scene_timeline.text_on_screen:
25 THINGS FOR FREELANCE CREATIVES
ORANGE TREE STUDIO
Subscribed

parsed_output.overall_summary: Creator @crsnscott promotes his free Substack newsletter, 'Orange Tree Studio,' specifically highlighting a post titled '25 Things for Freelance Creatives.' He walks through a curated list of resources he wishes he had when starting as a self-taught creative, including design tools like Cosmos and Framer, educational YouTube channels like The Futur, and business management tools like Hello Bonsai. The video serves as a resource guide and a call to action for viewers to subscribe to his weekly Wednesday newsletter for ongoing creative business tips.

takeaways.statement: Freelance creatives can significantly benefit from a curated list of tools for inspiration, learning, and business management.
The creator's Substack, Orange Tree Studio, provides these resources for free to help others build their creative businesses.
Continuous learning through specific YouTube channels and podcasts (like Rick Rubin's) is vital for creative growth.
